Ben Roethlisberger. An American quarterback who spent his entire eighteen-season career with the Pittsburgh Steelers, earning two Super Bowl championships and becoming one of the franchise's most successful modern passers. Known for his physical toughness and large stature at the position, he combined arm strength with mobility. Drafted first round, eleventh overall, in 2004 from Miami University, he became the youngest starting quarterback to win a Super Bowl in his second season. He won two Super Bowl championships: Super Bowl XL after the 2005 season and Super Bowl XLIII after 2008, both with the Steelers. He earned six Pro Bowl selections and two All-Pro selections during his career. Through his eighteen seasons, he threw for sixty-four thousand eighty-eight career passing yards and four hundred eighteen touchdowns, ranking among the franchise leaders and establishing himself as a consistent NFL performer. Known for his large frame at six feet five inches and two hundred forty pounds, he extended plays outside the pocket through physical mobility, creating opportunities through improvisation. He served as the Steelers' starting quarterback for all eighteen seasons from 2004 to 2021, unusual longevity with one franchise in the modern era, providing consistent leadership throughout two decades with Pittsburgh.
